record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports adding a harmful-minus-harmless mean-activation refusal direction to the residual stream and reports behavioral results on a new model. The result files listed in the repository indicate the evaluations were run.
record.gate_note: The README also reports a separate Function Vector intervention, RESTA, DARE, Safe LoRA, and a RESTA strength sweep; these do not test the specified single difference-in-means refusal direction and are not recorded as rows. The reported 79% harmless-refusal result was used to choose the steering layer, so it is not a row.
record.test_reason: Builds the harmful-minus-harmless mean-activation direction on a medical-fine-tuned Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct. Adding it to the residual stream at layer 18 on every prompt raises XSTest harmless refusals from 18.4% to 98% with MedQA unchanged. This tests V1's induction-by-addition part directly.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. Additions: the always-on direction refuses almost everything and is worse than RESTA. The gate costs nothing but gains nothing, because it fires on prompts already refused. The authors conclude a gate built on the model's own representation cannot catch its own misses.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a harmful-minus-harmless mean-activation direction and residual-stream addition, but applies it at selected layer 18 rather than testing ablation or interventions across every layer and position. Repository type: research/tool implementation.
record.method_sensitivity: Always-on versus gated application changes the outcome; the layer was selected using held-out harmless prompts.

fits_no_version.finding: Projection onto the direction at layer 18 flags 565 of 732 test prompts SFT refuses but only 1 of 238 it answers. It flags none of the 10 non-refused AdvBench requests. Authors: the direction separates will-refuse from will-not, not harmful from harmless.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The diff-in-means direction's projection tracks the model's refusal decision rather than prompt harmfulness, so it cannot flag harmful prompts the model fails to refuse.

record.problems: One model and one seed; the steering layer, coefficient, and gate threshold were selected once on validation prompts and not swept further. The always-on steering results are reported without uncertainty estimates in the comparison table.
record.rows_left_out: No README-reported results for the tested refusal direction were left out. Other method results were excluded because they do not test the specified direction.

untested.parts: Ablation (removing refusal) not tested. Addition only at one selected layer, one model, one coefficient. Other abilities checked only via MedQA letter accuracy.
No transfer test; the direction was computed on the fine-tuned model itself.
No comparison of training methods or stages.

missing.what: Gate flag rates by SFT refusal outcome: 565/732 refused vs 1/238 answered test prompts, 0/10 non-refused AdvBench. On validation: 72% harmful, 10.5% OR-Bench, 0% Alpaca.

record.verdict_notes: README only; one model, one seed. Layer 18 was chosen because it induced 79% harmless refusals on validation prompts, which is a selection value, not a row. Refusal is labelled by string-match and keyword checks.

versions.untested_parts: Tests adding the direction at one selected layer, not ablating it, adding it at every layer and position, or testing the full claim across other abilities.
The weight edits described are RESTA, DARE, and Safe LoRA, not abliteration.
Does not test jailbreak suppression of the direction or training against its ablation.
Does not test whether refusal is affine, a cone, or represented by multiple directions.
Does not measure an internal harmfulness judgment separately from the refusal decision.
Does not test transfer across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models.
Does not compare refusal training methods or stages.

relationships.condition: Always-on addition at layer 18, Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct after medical LoRA SFT
relationships.reason: Addition raises harmless refusals 46/250 to 245/250 (r1) and harmful refusals to 100% (r2, r3), while MedQA stays 48.0% vs 48.2% (r4).
relationships.display_finding: Addition increased harmless refusals from 46/250 to 245/250 and harmful refusal to 100%, while MedQA remained at 48.0% versus 48.2%.
